3. The petitioner as defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form as the prayers made therein are not tenable in law, the relationship between the petitioner-company and the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 was that of Master and Servant and hence a declaratory suit as framed is not maintainable in law, the prayer for reinstatement in service was beyond jurisdiction of the Civil Court and was not legally tenable. It was further stated that the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 was charged for misconduct by charge-sheet dated 6-6-1993 for misappropriation of Taka 2,107.68 by over writing, interpolation and falsifying the medical prescriptions given to him by company's doctor. The plaintiff-opposite party .submitted his explanation to the said charge-sheet by his letter dated 16-6-1993 in which he admitted the allegations of the said charge-sheet and prayed for exonerating him from the charges. The petitioner-company found him guilty on his admission and having regard to his past long service discharged him from service by order dated 7-7-1993 instead of dismissing him from service so that he may get some service benefits. The plaintiff-opposite party's application for reconsideration for his reinstatement in his service and his legal notice did not deserve any consideration and so those were rejected. There was no illegality in the action taken by the defendant petitioner-company against plaintiff-opposite party No. 1. With these assertions the petitioner-company prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. Admittedly, Padma Oil Ltd is a Public Ltd Company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. Admittedly, the same subsequently has been placed under the control, co-ordination and supervision of the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation pursuant to the provision of Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation Ordinance, 1976. Admittedly, the plaintiff was appointed as Accounts Officer on 2-5-1980 by Padma Oil Co Ltd and he served the defendant-petitioner company till he was discharged on 7-7-1993 on a charge of misconduct for misappropriation of money by falsifying, overwriting and interpolation of his medical prescription given by the petitioner company's doctor. Plaintiff challenged the said discharge order in the present suit.
